title: Kyivstar's Uklon Partners with OTP and ULF on New Car Leasing Solutions to Support Fleet Operators and Driver-Partners Across Ukraine
summary: Partnership introduces leasing solutions designed to support vehicle replacements, fleet expansion and business growth for Uklon's fleet operators KYIV, Ukraine and NEW YORK, July 22, 2026 - Kyivstar Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), the parent company of JSC Kyivstar (“Kyivstar”), Ukraine’s
body_text: Kyivstar's Uklon Partners with OTP and ULF on New Car Leasing Solutions to Support Fleet Operators and Driver-Partners Across Ukraine 22.07.2026 PDF Version Partnership introduces leasing solutions designed to support vehicle replacements, fleet expansion and business growth for Uklon's fleet operators KYIV, Ukraine and NEW YORK, July 22, 2026 - Kyivstar Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), the parent company of JSC Kyivstar (“Kyivstar”), Ukraine’s leading digital operator and part of VEON Group (Nasdaq: VEON), today announced that Uklon, Ukraine’s leading ride-sharing service and part of Kyivstar’s digital ecosystem, has entered into a partnership with OTP Bank, OTP Leasing and ULF to expand access to affordable credit and leasing solutions for fleet operators and driver-partners. "Uklon is committed to strengthening Ukraine's ride-hailing market, and that means meeting drivers and fleet operators where the need is greatest. Small and medium-sized businesses in particular need transparent, accessible financing to renew or grow their vehicle fleets during wartime,” said Ivan Chornohor, Vice President of Supply and Driver Operations at Uklon . “We're equally focused on supporting partners whose vehicles have been damaged or destroyed as a result of the war.” Under the partnership, Uklon fleet operators and driver-partners will have access to leasing solutions designed to support vehicle renewal, fleet expansion and business growth. The initiative is part of Uklon’s ongoing efforts to create new development opportunities for fleet operators and driver-partners, strengthening the foundation of the platform’s driver community as demand for ride-hailing and related mobility services continues to grow across Ukraine and allows Uklon to further grow its driver network and support the continued expansion of its marketplace. "OTP Bank is continuously moving forward: we are growing, expanding opportunities for our customers, and introducing new products. Today, OTP Bank is the market leader in financing pre-owned vehicles, but we are not stopping there. Our partnership with Uklon marks the next step in our strategic development. It brings together OTP Bank’s financial expertise and the innovation of one of the largest ride-hailing platforms, creating new opportunities for businesses and supporting the further development of the taxi services market", said Oleh Klymenko, Member of the Management Board of OTP Bank, responsible for Retail Banking. The leasing solutions are expected to be available directly through Uklon’s partner network, offering flexible terms tailored to the needs of both individual driver-partners and larger fleet operators. By lowering the barriers to acquiring and renewing vehicles, the partnership aims to help driver-partners maintain modern, reliable, and safe vehicles while enabling fleet operators to scale their operations more efficiently. "For OTP Leasing, today’s signing of the memorandum is a logical continuation of our mission: to make car financing accessible and flexible for businesses, including sole proprietors — who make up a significant share of Uklon’s driver-partners and fleet operators. Our partnership with Uklon allows us to directly support drivers and fleets — particularly those whose vehicles have been damaged as a result of Russian aggression. We offer them a practical tool for rapid recovery and fleet renewal, tailored specifically to the needs of small businesses and individual entrepreneurs. Better vehicles mean safer trips, greater comfort, and can contribute to lower environmental impact. I am confident that our joint work with Uklon will make these opportunities accessible to an even wider range of partners, regardless of the scale of their business", said Yanina Horenko, First Deputy CEO of OTP Leasing. “Since 2019, ULF has been financing vehicles for fleet operators working with ride-hailing platforms across Ukraine — from businesses with just a few cars to large fleets numbering in the hundreds. Over this period, we have financed more than 2,500 vehicles, while the largest fleet financed for a single partner comprises 1,000 cars. Our partnership with Uklon is a natural extension of this expertise and will enable us to extend financing solutions to even more entrepreneurs, helping them renew and expand their fleets without placing significant pressure on their working capital ”, said Dmytro Ulitin, Chief Commercial Officer of ULF . Integration with Uklon’s digital ecosystem is intended to streamline the leasing process, allowing eligible driver-partners and fleet operators to explore and manage leasing options as part of their existing relationship with the platform. About Uklon Uklon is a technology company that developed the eponymous mobile application. Founded in Kyiv in 2010, Uklon started as a ride-hailing platform and has evolved into a multi-service digital ecosystem integrating ride-hailing, Uklon Delivery, Uklon Ads, and the Uklon Travel bus ticket booking service. As of June 30, 2026, the Uklon service is available in 27 cities across Ukraine and at the Bukovel tourist complex. The company also operates in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. In April 2025, Uklon was acquired by JSC Kyivstar, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kyivstar Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: KYIV; KYIVW), whose shares are traded on the U.S. stock exchange Nasdaq and which is a part of the VEON Group. Official website: https://uklon.com.ua About Kyivstar Group Ltd. Kyivstar Group Ltd. (“Kyivstar Group”) is a Nasdaq-listed holding company that operates JSC Kyivstar, Ukraine’s leading digital operator and the first Ukrainian company to list on a U.S. stock exchange. Kyivstar Group companies provide a broad range of connectivity and digital services, including mobile and fixed-line voice and data, ride-hailing, e-health, digital TV, and enterprise solutions such as Big Data, cloud, and cybersecurity. For more information, please visit https://investors.kyivstar.ua . title: Fork data environments for DuckLake materialization
summary: Workspace forks now get an isolated data environment per DuckLake by default. Materializing pipelines in a fork write to a fork-scoped metadata schema and bucket prefix instead of the parent's tables, and tables the fork has not materialized yet are read from the parent through read-only defer views, so one node can be iterated on without rebuilding upstream. The fork-creation dialog adds a per-lake Isolated / Shared with parent choice, the pipeline graph shows deferred vs fork chips on DuckLake assets, and deleting a fork can drop its forked namespaces.
body_text: Fork data environments for DuckLake materialization Data pipelines Workspace Docs Workspace forks now get an isolated data environment per DuckLake by default. Materializing pipelines in a fork write to a fork-scoped metadata schema and bucket prefix instead of the parent's tables, and tables the fork has not materialized yet are read from the parent through read-only defer views, so one node can be iterated on without rebuilding upstream. The fork-creation dialog adds a per-lake Isolated / Shared with parent choice, the pipeline graph shows deferred vs fork chips on DuckLake assets, and deleting a fork can drop its forked namespaces. New features Forks default to an isolated data environment per lake: a fork-scoped metadata schema and a __wm_forks/<fork id>/ bucket prefix, with unchanged ducklake:// URIs and annotations Read-defer to the parent: tables the fork has not materialized are read through read-only views over the parent data, including the <table>_current companion view of SCD2 targets Parent lakes are attached read-only in forks, so a fork job cannot write parent data through DuckLake Fork-creation dialog gains a Ducklake data environment section with a per-lake Isolated (default) or Shared with parent choice; shared forks read and write the parent lake directly Pipeline graph marks each DuckLake asset in a fork with an amber deferred or emerald fork chip, with a matching banner in the details pane Fork deletion offers to drop forked DuckLake namespaces; also available as POST /w/<workspace>/workspaces/drop_forked_ducklake_namespaces

title: Rollforward in Accounting: Complete Guide for July 2026
summary: Learn how rollforward schedules track account movements from opening to closing balance. Complete guide to rollforward accounting for July 2026.
body_text: Month-end close is three days away. You're copying last period's rollforward template, pasting new GL data, updating formulas, and hoping nothing breaks. One cell reference moves and suddenly your debt schedule is off by $200,000. There's a better way to build rollforward schedules that doesn't rely on fragile spreadsheets and manual updates. Here's what finance teams are switching to. TLDR: A rollforward tracks account movement from opening to closing balance using Beginning Balance + Additions - Subtractions = Ending Balance Rollforwards explain change over time while reconciliations confirm accuracy at a single point Common types include fixed asset, AR, debt, deferred revenue, equity, and ARR schedules Auditors use roll forward procedures to extend interim testing through the financial statement date Double connects rollforward schedules to accounting systems with drill-down access to source transactions What Is a Rollforward in Accounting? A rollforward in accounting is a schedule that tracks how an account balance moves from one period to the next. Start with the opening balance, document every transaction and adjustment that occurred during the period, and arrive at the closing balance. The formula is: Beginning Balance + Additions - Subtractions = Ending Balance. That simple structure creates something valuable: an audit trail. Instead of comparing two numbers and wondering what happened between them, a rollforward shows exactly what moved an account from its starting point to its close. How Rollforward Accounting Works The process is sequential by design: Pull the prior period's closing balance as your opening figure Record each addition (purchases, period-end accruals, new debt issued) Record each subtraction (disposals, payments, amortization) Sum the activity to arrive at a closing balance Verify that closing balance matches your general ledger Every line in the schedule should tie back to a source document. That traceability is what makes the rollforward useful beyond basic record-keeping. When the closing balance agrees with your ledger, you have a clean, documented account history. When it doesn't, the schedule itself tells you exactly where to look for variance analysis . Rollforward vs. Reconciliation: Understanding the Difference Both terms come up constantly in accounting workflows, so the confusion is understandable. A rollforward tracks movement: it shows how a balance got from Point A to Point B over a period. A reconciliation confirms accuracy: it verifies that two independent records agree at a single point in time. The simplest way to think about it is that rollforwards explain change, while reconciliations confirm correctness. You often run both together, using the rollforward to build the ending balance and then tying that balance to an external source to catch any discrepancies. Common Rollforward Schedule Examples Rollforward schedules appear across nearly every area of accounting, each tracking a different account from opening to closing balance. Here are the most common types you'll encounter. Rollforward Type Opening Balance Common Additions Common Subtractions Primary Use Case Fixed Asset (PP&E) Prior period gross asset cost and accumulated depreciation of property, plant, and equipment Capital expenditures, asset acquisitions, construction in progress completions Asset disposals, depreciation expense, impairment charges Verify asset additions and retirements match capital expenditure authorizations and disposal proceeds Accounts Receivable Prior period ending AR balance from the balance sheet New customer invoices issued, accrued revenue recorded Cash collections received, bad debt write-offs, customer credits issued Track collectability and aging of outstanding customer balances Debt Prior period outstanding principal balance New borrowings, debt issuances, additional draws on credit facilities Principal repayments, debt extinguishments, amortization of issuance costs Monitor covenant compliance and verify principal movements tie to cash flow statement Deferred Revenue Prior period unearned revenue balance New customer prepayments collected, contract liabilities from new agreements Revenue recognized as performance obligations are satisfied Confirm revenue recognition timing aligns with contract terms and delivery milestones Equity Prior period stockholders equity from balance sheet Net income, stock issuances, additional paid-in capital from options exercised Dividends paid, share repurchases, treasury stock transactions Track all equity movements from the statement of stockholders equity ARR (SaaS) Prior period annual recurring revenue New bookings, customer expansions, upsells to existing accounts Customer churn, downgrades, contractions in subscription value Track predictable revenue streams and measure growth in subscription business models Fixed Asset (PP&E) Rollforward Starts with the opening net book value, adds capital expenditures, subtracts disposals, and deducts depreciation to arrive at the closing balance. Auditors rely on this to verify asset additions and retirements. Accounts Receivable Rollforward Tracks beginning AR, adds new invoices, subtracts cash collections and write-offs, and confirms the ending balance ties to the balance sheet. Debt Rollforward Schedule Opens with outstanding principal, adds new borrowings, removes repayments, and accounts for any amortization of debt issuance costs. Deferred Revenue Rollforward Begins with the prior period deferred balance, adds newly collected but unearned revenue , and subtracts amounts recognized as earned during the period. Building accurate deferred revenue schedules requires careful tracking of contract terms and performance obligation timing. Equity Rollforward Schedule Tracks opening stockholders equity through net income, dividends, share issuances, and repurchases to reach the closing equity balance. ARR Rollforward Common in SaaS finance, this tracks annual recurring revenue from the opening balance through new bookings, expansions, contractions, and churn to show net ARR movement. Fixed Asset Rollforward Schedules A fixed asset rollforward schedule tracks the movement of long-term assets across a reporting period. It starts with the opening balance of property, plant, and equipment, then layers in additions, disposals, depreciation, and impairments to arrive at the closing balance. Auditors rely on these schedules heavily. They verify that every addition ties to a capital expenditure authorization, disposals match proceeds recorded in cash, and accumulated depreciation is calculated correctly. Key Line Items in a PP&E Rollforward Opening gross asset balance per prior period financials Capital additions during the period, tied to invoices or capex approvals Disposals at cost, with corresponding removal of accumulated depreciation Depreciation expense for the period, verified against the income statement Closing net book value, which should agree to the balance sheet Rollforward Procedures in Audit Roll forward procedures are audit techniques used to extend the coverage of audit evidence from an interim testing date to the financial statement date. When auditors complete substantive testing before year-end, they need assurance that the account balances remain fairly stated through the reporting date. PCAOB Standards require these procedures for public companies to update interim testing results through year-end. There are several scenarios where roll forward procedures become necessary. When Auditors Use Roll Forward Procedures When interim audit work was performed months before the balance sheet date and conditions may have changed When testing manual controls, auditors perform roll forward procedures to confirm those controls remained effective through year-end When account balances tested at an interim date need validation through the final reporting period What Roll Forward Procedures Typically Involve Reviewing transactions that occurred between the interim testing date and year-end for unusual items or unexpected fluctuations Tying the interim tested balance to the year-end balance using a rollforward schedule Obtaining and testing additional samples from the roll forward period when risk warrants it Confirming that no major changes in internal controls occurred after interim testing was completed The roll forward period refers to the gap between the interim audit date and the financial statement date. The longer this gap, the more substantive the roll forward procedures typically need to be. Why Rollforward Reports Matter for Financial Reporting Rollforward reports give finance teams and auditors a structured way to verify that account balances move correctly from one period to the next. Without them, it becomes nearly impossible to spot where a discrepancy originated or whether a closing balance was accurately carried forward. For auditors, rollforward schedules are a core part of year-end testing. They confirm that interim audit work still holds by the time financial statements are issued. For controllers and CFOs, they serve as a real-time check on whether the numbers tell a consistent story across periods with close management tools. Best Practices for Creating Rollforward Schedules A well-structured rollforward schedule does more than track numbers. It creates a clear audit trail and keeps your financial reporting defensible under scrutiny. Here are the practices that separate reliable schedules from ones that create problems later: Start with a verified opening balance that ties directly to the prior period's closing balance, confirmed and signed off by the appropriate reviewer using close management systems . Use a consistent format across all schedules so that anyone reviewing the file can follow the logic without needing a walkthrough. Document every line item with a source reference, whether that's a journal entry number, invoice, or supporting sub-schedule. Verify the closing balance against the general ledger before the schedule is considered complete, not after review comments come in. Date-stamp all updates and track who made changes, especially in shared files where multiple team members contribute. Flag unusual movements, such as large unexplained decreases or activity that falls outside normal patterns, with a brief explanatory note directly in the schedule. Common Rollforward Mistakes and How to Avoid Them A few mistakes show up repeatedly across rollforward schedules, and each one undermines what the schedule is supposed to accomplish. Removing only net book value on disposals instead of eliminating both gross asset cost and accumulated depreciation separately. This inflates both balance sheet line items and creates ghost balances that compound over time. Missing the reversal of a prior period accrual, which double-counts the expense and distorts the opening balance before a single new transaction is added. Timing differences where activity posts in the wrong period, so the schedule closes clean but against an incorrect number. Copying GL output line-for-line without a validation step. A rollforward that simply mirrors the ledger doesn't verify anything, which is why validation steps are required before finalizing any schedule. That last issue points to something worth stating plainly: a rollforward without supporting documentation is not a true reconciliation. It records what happened. It doesn't confirm that what happened was correct. Automating Rollforward Accounting for Month-End Close Manual rollforward preparation is repetitive by nature. You pull data from one system, paste it into a spreadsheet, apply formulas, and hope nothing breaks when you update the next period. When source systems change, every formula becomes suspect. Connecting rollforward schedules directly to accounting systems removes that problem through automated month-end close management . Additions and subtractions post automatically as transactions hit the ledger, balances update in real time, and the risk of a copy-paste error quietly corrupting your schedule disappears with it. The bigger gain shows up during review. Instead of flipping between schedules and source documents, you can drill from a summary balance down to the individual transaction behind it in seconds. Auditors asking about a specific line item? The answer is one click away, not a 30-minute reconstruction. Building Better Rollforwards with Double's Month-End Close Management Rollforward schedules sit at the intersection of accuracy and speed, and getting them right under close deadlines is genuinely hard. Double's month-end close management is built around exactly this kind of work, helping finance teams move through their rollforward schedules without losing track of supporting detail or version history. Instead of chasing down numbers across spreadsheets, teams can work through rollforwards in one place , with clear audit trails that hold up to scrutiny during review. Final Thoughts on Rollforward Documentation Rollforwards prove how balances moved, which matters more than most people realize until an auditor asks for backup on a three-month-old transaction. Tools that connect rollforward accounting schedules directly to your ledger eliminate the version control issues and formula errors that slow down close cycles. You don't need perfect schedules on day one, but you do need a system that gets better each period. Build the habits now, and your close process will get faster without cutting corners.

title: Dream Finders Appoints Steve Fischer to its Board of Directors
summary: JACKSONVILLE, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (the “Company,” “Dream Finders” or “DFH”) (NYSE: DFH), announced…...
body_text: Dream Finders Appoints Steve Fischer to its Board of Directors July 17, 2026 7:00am EDT Download as PDF JACKSONVILLE, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (the “Company,” “Dream Finders” or “DFH”) (NYSE: DFH), announced today the appointment of Steve Fischer to the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board of Directors” or “Board”). Mr. Fischer will serve on the Audit Committee of the Board. Mr. Fischer brings more than thirty years of executive leadership experience in banking, financial services and public accounting to our Board of Directors. He is currently the President of The Pitney Bowes Bank, a subsidiary of Pitney Bowes Inc. (NYSE: PBI). Previously, he served as President and Chief Executive Officer of TIAA Bank after holding roles of President, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer. Prior to that, Mr. Fischer served as Chief Financial Officer of EverBank Financial Corp. (formerly NYSE: EVER), where he played a key role in the company’s growth and public company operations. Before joining EverBank in 2011, Mr. Fischer spent more than 18 years with Deloitte & Touche LLP, ultimately serving as a Partner for a variety of clients including several Fortune 100 entities, as well as mid-sized banks and mortgage companies. Mr. Fischer adds extensive expertise in corporate finance, capital markets and risk management to our Board of Directors. Mr. Fischer earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Accounting and Finance from Florida State University and is a licensed Certified Public Accountant in Florida. Patrick Zalupski, Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Chairman of Dream Finders, commented, “Steve’s appointment represents another important step in the thoughtful evolution of our Board. His extensive financial, banking and public company expertise will bring valuable perspective to the Board as we continue pursuing our strategic priorities and evaluating opportunities for further growth.” Mr. Fischer added, “I am honored to join Dream Finders’ Board of Directors at such an important time in the Company’s growth. Dream Finders has built an impressive platform and disciplined financial approach. I look forward to working with the Board and the management team to drive long-term value for the shareholders.” About Dream Finders Homes, Inc. Dream Finders Homes (NYSE: DFH), headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, was recognized as the 2025 National Builder of the Year by Builder magazine. Dream Finders Homes builds single-family homes throughout the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, including Florida, Texas, Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Colorado, Arizona, and the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, which comprises Washington D.C., Northern Virginia and Maryland. As the Official Home Builder of the PGA TOUR, the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Tampa Bay Rays, Dream Finders Homes is deeply committed to excellence beyond homebuilding and into the communities it serves. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, DFH also provides mortgage financing as well as title agency and underwriting services to homebuyers. Dream Finders Homes achieves its growth and returns by maintaining an asset-light homebuilding model. For more information, please visit www.dreamfindershomes.com . Released July 17, 2026

title: Harmonic Commits $25,000 to Venezuela Earthquake Relief Efforts in Partnership with Global Empowerment Mission
summary: Harmonic donates $25,000 to support earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela through Global Empowerment Mission, aiding communities in urgent need.
body_text: San Jose, CA — July 16, 2026 — Harmonic (NASDAQ: HLIT) today announced a $25,000 donation to Global Empowerment Mission (GEM) in support of ongoing earthquake relief operations in Venezuela. The contribution is designated exclusively for GEM's Venezuela Earthquake Relief program and is intended to sustain the organization's immediate distribution of emergency supplies to affected communities. “When disaster strikes in a region where our customers, partners and colleagues live and work, we want to support by acting quickly,” said Nimrod Ben-Natan, President and CEO of Harmonic. “The people of Venezuela need support right now. Partnering with an organization like GEM, which has trusted networks and resources on the ground, is the most direct way we can ensure our contribution translates into real relief.” GEM's response teams are operating across Venezuela's hardest-hit areas to coordinate the distribution of medical supplies, clean water and hygiene kits. Harmonic's funding is directed toward sustaining these operations at a critical stage of the relief effort. “In the wake of such catastrophic seismic destruction, speed and trusted logistics are everything to the families who have lost their homes,” said Michael Capponi, President and Founder of Global Empowerment Mission. “Corporate partners stepping up with immediate funding is what allows our recon and emergency response teams to keep packing and distributing vital supplies directly into the hardest-hit communities. We are grateful to Harmonic for this timely support, which directly fuels our ability to stabilize these neighborhoods alongside our local partners.” To learn more about GEM's Venezuela earthquake relief operations or to make a donation, visit www.globalempowermentmission.org . More information about Harmonic is available at www.harmonicinc.com . About Harmonic Harmonic (NASDAQ: HLIT), the worldwide leader in virtualized broadband solutions, is transforming multi-gigabit connectivity. The company’s industry-leading cOS™ virtualized broadband platform, suite of solutions for fiber and DOCSIS, and a growing portfolio of AI-powered network intelligence solutions, enable broadband service providers to simplify operations, deliver exceptional subscriber experiences and expand revenue streams. With thousands of vCMTS servers and hundreds of thousands of RPDs deployed globally, Harmonic powers next-generation broadband services with five-nines reliability. Anchored with a customer-first approach and driven by a legacy of innovation, Harmonic supports broadband service providers at every stage of their network evolution. More information is available at www.harmonicinc.com . Harmonic, the Harmonic logo and other Harmonic marks are owned by Harmonic Inc. or its affiliates. All other trademarks referenced herein are the property of their respective owners.

title: The Digital Nomad Diary: How to Pack an Office in a Tote Bag
summary: By Gabriel Costa, Head of Marketing for Mobile & Audio Solutions There's a version of this summer where you're not chained to a desk. Where ‘the office’ is a blanket in Hyde Park, a café table in Barcelona or a beachside warung in Bali. The work is the same. The location doesn't have to be. [...]
body_text: By Gabriel Costa, Head of Marketing for Mobile & Audio Solutions There’s a version of this summer where you’re not chained to a desk. Where ‘the office’ is a blanket in Hyde Park, a café table in Barcelona or a beachside warung in Bali. The work is the same. The location doesn’t have to be. What stops most people isn’t the job. It’s the gear. Laptop bags that wreck your shoulders. Mice that need a flat, clean surface that doesn’t exist in the wild. Keyboards that take up half the table. The hardware hasn’t caught up with the lifestyle or, at least, most of it hasn’t. Here’s a few tips on how to build a setup that genuinely fits in a tote bag, without compromising on the stuff that actually matters. Step 1: Start with the bag, not the gear Most people pack first and regret it at the airport. Start by picking a tote or daypack with a slim internal sleeve, something designed for a tablet or 13-inch laptop. That sleeve becomes the structural spine of your whole setup. Everything else has to earn its place around it. If it doesn’t fit flat, it doesn’t come. Step 2: Sort the keyboard situation This is where most mobile setups fall apart. A full-size keyboard with unprotected keys is a non-starter. But typing on a laptop keyboard for eight hours straight on a café table that wobbles isn’t a solution either. Mobile keyboards like the Logitech Keys-To-Go 2 are worth knowing about here. Many are genuinely thin, about the width of a pencil, and slip into a tablet sleeve without adding meaningful bulk. Multi-device Bluetooth means you can hop between your laptop, iPad and phone without re-pairing every time. Battery life is measured in months, not days, which matters when you’re not near a desk drawer full of charging cables. If you’re working primarily from an iPad, using the Logitech Combo Touch is a different proposition entirely. It is a keyboard case that turns your iPad into something that functions like a laptop, with a trackpad included, and folds away when you’re done. Or for a seamless blend of work and play, you may want to try the Flip Folio , a keyboard case featuring a detachable keyboard for iPad Pro and iPad Air. Whether you’re binge-watching, scrolling through social media or checking emails, Flip Folio keeps you connected wherever life takes you. Step 3: The mouse question Plenty of people try to go mouse free when they’re working on the move. It’s one less thing to carry, and a trackpad feels like it should be enough. For a couple of emails, maybe it is. For a full working day with spreadsheets, editing and anything that needs precision, you’ll feel the difference by lunchtime. The new Mobi Fold ultra portable mouse folds to the size of a post-it note and slips into your pocket or travel bag and was designed for working on-the-go. For something truly minimalist, a compact option like the Logitech Pebble Mouse 2 M350S fits right in the palm of your hand and is light enough to forget it’s even in your bag. Both options also feature quiet clicks, which matters immensely when you’re working in a hushed café at 9 AM. If your work demands more precision, something like the MX Anywhere 3S is built for the wild; it tracks seamlessly on virtually any surface, including glass, so that polished marble café table won’t bring your workday to a halt. All of these mice connect via Bluetooth or the USB receiver and last months on a single charge. Pick based on how much precision and portability you actually need. Step 4: Fix the surface problem Here’s the thing nobody tells you about working outdoors: public surfaces are rarely inviting. Even if your mouse can handle the tracking, a rustic wooden picnic bench offers a bumpy ride, a beach bar counter is prone to condensation rings and a metal park table gets boiling hot by noon. A rollable fabric desk mat solves this completely. It weighs almost nothing, rolls up to roughly the size of a water bottle, and turns whatever surface you land on into a clean, consistent tracking zone. Splinters, grain, bumps; none of it matters anymore. It’s the least glamorous item in the bag and possibly the most useful one. Step 5: The stuff people forget A few things that don’t take up much space but make a real difference: A multi-port wall charger. Most café tables have one power outlet and it’s never near you. A multi-port charger with USB-A & USB-C ports buys you options. A book under the back edge to elevate your screen. Neck angle matters when you’re working for hours. Your future self will thank you. Headphones, obviously. But a small pouch to keep cables and adapters from becoming a tangled mess at the bottom of the bag, super easy and very underrated. The full kit, at a glance The goal is a setup that is lightweight and clears security without drama. Laptop, Keys-To-Go 2 or Combo Touch or Flip Folio if you’re iPad-first, Mobi Fold, Pebble Mouse 2 M350S or MX Anywhere 3S depending on your needs, rollable desk mat, multi-port charger, notebook, sleeve pouch. That’s it. You don’t need less ambition this summer. Hyde Park, Barcelona, Bali: the office is wherever you open the bag. Gabriel Costa is head of marketing for Logitech’s Mobile & Audio Solutions business and can be found working at a cafe with his cappuccino, laptop, Mobi Fold and Keys-to-Go 2 quite often.

title: Scientist Warns Popular Children's Drinks Could Raise Blood Pressure Risk Later in Life

body_text: A new long-term study suggests sugary drinks and excessive fruit juice consumption during childhood may increase the risk of high blood pressure in adulthood. Learn what the research found and why experts recommend healthier alternatives. Sugary drinks have long been linked to obesity, diabetes, and tooth decay. Now, new research suggests they may also increase the risk of developing high blood pressure later in life, especially when these beverages become a regular part of a child's diet. Researchers say dietary habits formed during childhood can influence long-term cardiovascular health. The findings highlight the importance of encouraging healthier drink choices from an early age to reduce future health risks. The study, published in the American Heart Association's journal Circulation , found that children and teenagers who regularly consumed sugary beverages were significantly more likely to develop high blood pressure as adults. Long-Term Study Reveals Strong Link The research followed 25,749 participants as part of the Growing Up Today Study (GUTS) . Participants completed detailed health and dietary questionnaires every one to four years, with some individuals being monitored for up to 25 years . Researchers tracked the consumption of several popular beverages, including: Soft drinks and soda Lemonade Sweetened tea Sports drinks Fruit juice Other beverages and foods The study also considered body weight, physical activity, smoking habits, and other lifestyle factors to better understand how beverage choices influenced future health outcomes. Higher Intake Meant Higher Risk According to the researchers, individuals who consumed more than two servings of sugary drinks per day had a 52 percent higher risk of developing high blood pressure later in life compared with those who drank fewer than three servings each week. The increased risk varied depending on the type of beverage consumed. Researchers reported that: Drinking soda every day was linked to a 23 percent higher risk of high blood pressure. Consuming one serving of sports drinks daily was associated with a 36 percent higher risk . Drinking more than 1.5 servings of fruit juice each day increased the risk by 35 percent compared with people who drank less than one serving per week. For the purposes of the study, one serving was defined as an 8-ounce (240 ml) drink. Fruit Juice Is Not Always a Healthy Choice Many parents consider fruit juice to be a healthier alternative to soda. While 100 percent fruit juice does contain vitamins and nutrients, researchers say moderation is still important. Senior study author Vasanti Malik , an associate professor at the University of Toronto , explained that low levels of fruit juice may not be harmful, but consuming large amounts regularly could contribute to increased health risks. She emphasized that whole fruit should generally be chosen instead of juice because it contains fiber, which slows sugar absorption and supports overall health. Swapping Sugary Drinks for Fruit May Help The study also found encouraging evidence that replacing sugary beverages with whole fruit could make a meaningful difference. Researchers estimated that replacing one serving of a sugary drink each day with one serving of whole fruit could reduce the risk of developing high blood pressure by approximately 22 percent . Whole fruits provide vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and dietary fiber while typically containing less concentrated sugar than fruit juice. Health experts continue to recommend water and milk as the primary drinks for children, with sugary beverages reserved only for occasional consumption. Why Childhood Habits Matter High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, has traditionally been considered an adult condition. However, healthcare professionals are increasingly diagnosing elevated blood pressure in teenagers and even younger children. According to Prof. Malik, this trend makes early prevention especially important. Healthy eating habits established during childhood often continue into adulthood. Regular consumption of sugary beverages may contribute to weight gain, insulin resistance, and other metabolic changes that increase the likelihood of developing cardiovascular disease later in life. Reducing added sugar intake during childhood could therefore have benefits that extend well beyond adolescence. Researchers Urge Caution Although the findings are significant, the researchers caution that the study does not prove sugary drinks directly cause high blood pressure. The research relied on participants reporting their own dietary habits and medical diagnoses through questionnaires. Self-reported data can sometimes be inaccurate due to memory errors or reporting bias. In addition, other lifestyle or genetic factors that were not fully measured may have influenced participants' blood pressure over time. Because the study was observational, it identifies an association rather than a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Researchers say additional clinical studies are needed to better understand exactly how sugary beverages influence blood pressure throughout life. Practical Tips for Parents Parents looking to support their children's long-term heart health may consider a few simple changes: Encourage water as the primary beverage throughout the day. Limit sugary drinks such as soda, sports drinks, and sweetened teas. Offer whole fruit instead of fruit juice whenever possible. Keep portion sizes of 100 percent fruit juice small. Read nutrition labels to identify added sugars in beverages. Set a positive example by choosing healthier drinks yourself. Small dietary changes during childhood may have lasting benefits for cardiovascular health later in life. The Bottom Line This long-term study adds to growing evidence that sugary drinks may have lasting effects beyond weight gain and dental health. Researchers found that children who regularly consumed sugary beverages, including large amounts of fruit juice, faced a higher risk of developing high blood pressure as adults. While the study does not establish direct causation, experts agree that limiting sugary drinks and encouraging healthier alternatives such as water and whole fruit is a practical step families can take to support lifelong heart health. Sources Malik V. et al. Circulation , American Heart Association. Study examining childhood sugary beverage intake and later risk of hypertension. American Heart Association. Growing Up Today Study (GUTS). The Independent (July 24, 2026). Disclaimer This article is intended for informational and educational purposes only and should not be considered medical advice. The findings discussed are based on observational research, which identifies associations rather than proving cause and effect. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before making significant dietary or health decisions for yourself or your child.

All blogs Company Retail Restaurant Ecommerce Golf Retail What Growth-Minded Retailers Are Doing After the NetSuite POS & SCIS Sunset by Alyssa Albanese 2026-07-20 minute read Share Post Oracle’s upcoming sunset of NetSuite POS and SuiteCommerce InStore (SCIS) has forced a sudden pivot for many retailers. While an unexpected software migration like this is always a major disruption, it’s also a massive strategic opportunity. Forward-thinking retailers won’t simply be scrambling for a quick, 1:1 POS replacement. They’ll use this moment to re-evaluate their entire commerce stack, and ensure they’re making the right decisions for the next decade of retail. With that said, we’ve identified three core areas that retailers should prioritize as they plan their post-sunset roadmaps. Keep reading as we outline these priorities and uncover critical considerations that will be important as you navigate this transition yourself. Priority 1: Strengthening ERP-connected operations For any enterprise retailer, the NetSuite ERP acts as the ultimate source of truth for financials, procurement and high-level inventory tracking. The biggest risk during a platform swap is degrading that source of truth by introducing data silos or fragile integration layers. Growth-minded brands should filter their software search through a strict operational lens, focusing on three specific criteria: Real-time, bidirectional sync: When an item sells in store, a purchase order is adjusted or a return is processed, that data needs to sync with NetSuite immediately. Retailers should prioritize platforms that offer live, two-way syncing so that teams always have an accurate, real-time view of their inventory and profitability. Eliminating custom code middleware: Custom-built API integrations are expensive to build and highly fragile. To mitigate implementation risk, companies should prioritize platforms with native or deeply established NetSuite connectors—specifically those carrying official Built for NetSuite (BFN) certification. This ensures the integration meets Oracle’s enterprise standards for security without requiring internal teams to maintain custom code. Protecting business continuity: A successful transition means front-of-house staff experience zero friction or learning curves on day one of the new system, while back-of-house teams see a clean continuation of automatic transaction matching, tax management and cash reconciliation. Migrate to a BFN-Certified POS without the risk Lightspeed Retail for NetSuite is a BFN-certified solution that brings front-of-house and back-of-house operations together seamlessly. It automates the flow of inventory, financial and customer data between your stores and your ERP, maintaining real-time accuracy and eliminating manual work. Transition from NSPOS or SCIS to Lightspeed while maintaining NetSuite as your single source of truth . Start up quickly without the need for complex re-platforming, and minimize disruptions with expert-supported onboarding. “Lightspeed and NetSuite enable growth, great customer experiences, great employee experiences and overall operational excellence.” Joel Allen, Director of Business Acceleration, Atlas Tools & Machinery Learn more about Lightspeed Retail for NetSuite. Priority 2: Unifying retail, omnichannel and wholesale ecosystems Consumers rarely interact with their favorite brands through a single channel. And many NetSuite users already run highly complex operations that span brick-and-mortar, ecommerce, B2B and more. Legacy retail systems would force these environments into separate operational silos, creating a disjointed flow of data back to the central ERP. But this doesn’t work for modern retailers and especially not for those that plan to scale. To build a truly unified commerce model that works now and in the future, brands should leverage this migration period as an opportunity to clean up their infrastructure with seamlessly connected tech. Gaining a complete, transparent view of inventory Managing inventory across a modern retail business of any size requires complete, real-time visibility across every physical storefront, warehouse and digital sales channel. Without this, execution falls short and leads to detrimental out-of-stock or oversold scenarios. During this migration period, retailers should prioritize systems that seamlessly bridge their physical store stock with their digital storefronts. These modern systems ensure that exact, live inventory counts are accessible across all locations simultaneously. This is crucial to executing omnichannel fulfillment options like buy online, pick up in store (BOPIS), curbside pickup or ship-from-store, for example. Connecting customer journeys Customers expect their brand relationship to be recognized everywhere. If a customer accumulates loyalty points online or updates their profile details via their mobile device, that data should be instantly accessible to an associate on the physical showroom floor. True cross-channel visibility empowers associates to sell more and drives retention, making it an essential consideration during this migration period. Bridging the retail and wholesale divide For scaling brands, the purchasing side of retail is historically fragmented. Buyers spend hours flipping through catalogs, manually drafting purchase orders and hand-keying new stock descriptions once shipments arrive. As you migrate from NSPOS or SCSIS to another system, you don’t have to maintain this same disconnected process. A solution like Lightspeed Retail for NetSuite has a built-in wholesale network, allowing buyers to view live supplier catalogs and generate POs directly from sales reports. Because the system is built to organize complex inventory—including high-volume SKUs, variants and serialized items—retailers gain clear visibility into exact stock counts across every stockroom, warehouse and digital storefront. When a shipment arrives, staff can simply scan it in to update counts across all locations, and automatically update values in NetSuite. What’s more, access to live sales data and trend insights make it easier to forecast seasonal demand and identify bestsellers early. By pairing these insights with automated low-stock alerts and preset reorder points, retailers can keep shelves balanced, improve sell-through and reduce deadstock without additional manual work. “I love the fact that if we go into NetSuite and we enter a PO, we can send it to Lightspeed instantly.” Michael Slagle, Vice President of Retail Operations, Imagine Exhibitions Learn more about Lightspeed Wholesale. Priority 3: Scalability beyond immediate needs With a sunset deadline approaching, it’s easy to fall into the trap of picking a POS platform just to cross it off your to-do list. However, switching your front-of-house infrastructure is a major investment of time, resources and capital. Having to repeat the entire process three years from now because your business outgrew a short-sighted solution is an operational failure. Retailers focused on sustainable, long-term expansion are evaluating potential software partners based on their capacity for future scale. They’ll be considering: Geographic and location flexibility: Opening a new permanent location, launching a seasonal pop-up or expanding into a new international market shouldn’t require your IT department to start from scratch. Growth-minded retailers are looking for platforms that enable them to add new sales channels or physical locations seamlessly. The connection to your NetSuite ERP should be plug-and-play, automatically adapting to your new locations without requiring expensive custom workarounds. Unlocking richer, multi-store insights: While the ERP remains the system of record for macro financials, store managers and regional directors need clear and accessible analytics to make day-to-day decisions. Growth-minded retailers should choose platforms that deliver robust yet intuitive reports on product performance and staff scheduling to help their teams at the store level. The strategic path forward The retailers that will benefit most from the end of NetSuite POS and SCIS are those who refuse to treat the sunset like any other IT chore. By looking beyond a simple software swap, these brands will set themselves up for years of supported growth. They’re choosing platforms that streamline processes and eliminate tedious admin tasks, so their staff can spend less time fixing data errors and more time doing what they do best. As you map out your transition timeline, look for a partner that respects NetSuite as your undisputed system of record, while delivering a world-class, intuitive front-of-house experience for both staff and customers. Lightspeed helps ambitious mid-market and enterprise brands navigate this pivot with integrated solutions that are built to last. As a BFN-certified partner, Lightspeed bridges advanced retail POS, multichannel ecommerce and a native wholesale network directly into your NetSuite environment. By automating data flows and protecting your ERP investment, Lightspeed helps you turn a mandatory technical migration into your business’s next competitive advantage.
